rows.title: What’s Working: How Colorado’s wages increased for 10 years — until they were adjusted for inflation

rows.title: Pepper Pong — pickleball and pingpong’s baby — is a new game helping people get sober

rows.title: What’s Working: The future of Colorado Springs’ economy and what it takes to live there
rows.standfirst: Economic development has helped the region stay ahead of the nation but with advances, there are growing pains, like keeping housing affordable for the needed workers.

rows.title: New Belgium Brewing prepares for industrial heat pump that could cut its greenhouse gas emissions

rows.title: Why did Centura Health’s partners break up? “They just weren’t on the same page,” former CEO says.

rows.title: Medical debt nearly pushed a Colorado family onto the streets

rows.title: A Colorado dad wanted more for his son. So he opened a trade school for young adults with autism.

rows.title: Coloradans are projected to receive slightly lower taxpayer refunds next year than anticipated
rows.standfirst: The Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights refunds will be slightly lower in part because there was an increased number of people filing 2022 tax returns, meaning the refund dollars are being spread thinner than anticipated

rows.title: Work 4 days, get paid for 5: Why some Colorado companies are moving to a 4-day workweek
rows.standfirst: Shorter workweeks attract employees while employers cite benefits, like retention and recruitment. But a 32-hour week may not be for everyone.

rows.title: Feds give Xcel $70 million for innovative clean energy storage in Colorado and Minnesota

rows.title: Telluride is among the first Colorado mountain towns to consider easing short-term rental restrictions

rows.title: Sewer gas leaked into their condo for 9 months. It could have been different under Denver’s new rental law.

rows.title: There’s been a surge of abandoned oil and gas wells in Colorado over the past 90 days
